claim: Regulated stablecoin rails may create a second programmable dollar settlement layer and additional demand channel for short-term U.S. debt, while still depending on banks, regulators, reserves, AML/sanctions compliance, and Treasury-market liquidity.
funding_chain: GENIUS Act creates permitted payment stablecoin issuer framework
OCC/FDIC/Fed issue implementation rules for supervised entities
Permitted issuers hold reserves in cash, Treasuries, repo
Stablecoin growth creates demand for short-term dollar safe assets
Programmable settlement rails reduce legacy bottleneck friction

counter_thesis.description: Regulation concentrates power in permitted issuers and banks
counter_thesis.mitigation: Multiple issuer framework reduces single-point concentration

counter_thesis.description: Stablecoins not FDIC insured; reserve run risk
counter_thesis.mitigation: 100% reserve backing with liquid assets mitigates but does not eliminate

counter_thesis.description: Stablecoin Treasury demand too small relative to total US debt
counter_thesis.mitigation: Marginal demand matters at auction; growth trajectory matters

counter_thesis.description: Foreign regulatory pushback on dollar stablecoin dominance
counter_thesis.mitigation: GENIUS Act is US domestic framework; foreign jurisdictions build own

disconfirming_evidence: GENIUS Act implementation rules block most issuers
Major stablecoin reserve failure or bank run
Stablecoin market cap stagnates or declines for 2+ years
Treasury auctions show no correlation with stablecoin reserve growth
